exposure: Major obstetric haemorrhage characteristics (e.g., estimated blood loss, cause like uterine atony)
Management strategies (e.g., uterotonic agent use, blood transfusion)
cohort: The study included reported cases of major obstetric haemorrhage in Irish maternity units, with denominator data restricted to live births and stillbirths.
finding: During 2011-2018, there was a 54% increase in Major Obstetric Haemorrhage, a 60% increase in Postpartum Haemorrhage, and a 54% increase in blood transfusion in Irish maternity units.
mod_finding: At least one uterotonic agent was used to arrest bleeding in 94% of the 477 MOH cases associated with a vaginal or caesarean delivery.
